_note: Station settings. Copy to config/bandwatch.json and edit. Anything with no safe default is either absent here or null, and the code refuses to start rather than guessing -- a guessed value does not fail, it answers questions about somewhere you are not.

station._note: REQUIRED. Your receiver's position. ADS-B distance rules and satellite pass prediction are measured from this point. Precision beyond about 3 decimal places buys you nothing and tells strangers where you live: 43.65 is a city, 43.6501234 is a house.

_timezone_note: An IANA zone, e.g. America/Denver or Europe/Berlin. Quiet hours are wall-clock, local: applying a UTC 'quiet after 22:00' rule to a local station silences the wrong six hours.
_learning_note: On a fresh install every signal is novel, so novelty alerting stays suppressed for this many hours while a baseline forms. Watch the suppression actually fire before trusting it -- a guard you have never seen work is not a guard.
_notify_enabled_note: Alerting is OFF by default. Turn it on only once you have watched the rules fire in the console and agree with them; an alert path you have not calibrated trains you to ignore it, and then the one that mattered arrives and nothing happens.
_notifier_note: One of: none, webhook, command. See notify/README.md to add another.

command._note: Run a program with the alert JSON on stdin. This is how you reach anything with a CLI -- signal-cli, ntfy, a pager gateway, a shell script. argv is a LIST, never a shell string: alerts carry text that arrived over the air from someone you do not control.

_no_notify_note: Rules listed here are still RECORDED and still shown in the console; only the push is withheld. Withheld is a DISTINCT state from undelivered -- conflating them makes a backlog that grows forever and means nothing. A station near a busy airport probably wants low_aircraft and notable_aircraft in here.
_transcribe_note: Speech-to-text is OFF by default because it is the one part of this system that can invent evidence. Read docs/COVERAGE.md before enabling it. Whisper hallucinates confidently on silence: 30 s of noise became 'Thank you.', and 59% of airband transcripts on this author's station were fabrication.
_transcribe_mode_note: watchwords = transcribe only clips whose cheap pass suggests a watchlist term; all = transcribe everything (expensive, and far more fabrication to filter).
_adsb_below_note: Absolute MSL altitude below which an aircraft counts as low. Set it to your local ground elevation plus adsb_alert_agl_ft -- ADS-B reports MSL, so a flat AGL threshold is wrong by exactly your elevation. Leave null to compute it from station.alt_m.
_airport_note: Aircraft within this many nautical miles of the airport are landing or departing, not loitering. Without it, every approach looks like an event. Null disables the exclusion.
_models_note: Summarisation only, never ingest. No model sits in the detection path, so events keep logging when every model host is down. DSP detects; the model only summarises.
_sat_note: Weather-satellite capture is off by default for two reasons. NOAA-15/18/19 APT are all decommissioned (2025). And an indoor dipole cannot do LRPT: an 82-degree METEOR-M2 pass measured 1.6 dB SNR against the 6-8 dB needed, BER 0.41, and decoded zero bytes in 17 minutes. Note that a VERTICAL dipole NULLS AT ZENITH, so a high pass is its worst case, not its best -- 'wait for a better pass' is backwards indoors. A QFH or turnstile outdoors is the real fix.
